alternatives.root_cause: checkout exhausted threads or connections waiting on payment
alternatives.why_not: No change on checkout and the latency is confined to a single outbound hop, not spread across all of checkout's calls.

alternatives.root_cause: payment is partitioned from the network
alternatives.why_not: payment's spans still complete quickly and successfully; traffic flows, it is merely delayed by a fixed 300ms shaper.

verdict.summary: A traffic-shaping sidecar attached to payment's network namespace added a 300ms delay on eth0, so checkout's Charge calls waited ~300ms in network time while payment's own handler stayed fast.
verdict.reasoning: checkout's error ratio did not depart from baseline (tr_e7d2aa6a4cee), so this is a latency incident, not an error one. In tr_e14c66103740 the dominant hop is checkout's client span for PaymentService/Charge at ~300-310ms of self-time, while payment's own server and charge spans are ~1ms - the time is spent on the wire, outside payment's handler. checkout itself had no changes (tr_b711513b5687), while payment shows a traffic-shaping container attached to its network namespace imposing a 300ms eth0 delay just before the slow traces (tr_d292182561d1). A setting that inserts delay into a call path is dependency_latency, with checkout the service that merely noticed.
open_questions: Whether the delay was intentional (chaos experiment) or an automation error
Whether other callers of payment were affected and whether any checkouts actually timed out, since error ratio stayed flat
